claims.explanation: Fenbendazole is a benzimidazole tubulin-polymerization inhibitor whose selectivity likely reflects dependence on microtubule dynamics for mitosis and on tubulin/microtubule-binding drug efflux or resistance mechanisms. Lines with high TUBB/tubulin expression and rapid proliferation, or with loss of p53-mediated apoptosis, may be more sensitive, while high ABCB1/MDR1 efflux or low tubulin dependence confers protection. The transcriptional signature (down STMN1, TOP2A, CDK1, UBE2C; similarity to microtubule inhibitors) supports a mitotic/antimitotic mechanism.

features.basis: drug target; higher tubulin levels increase benzimidazole binding and microtubule disruption
microtubule-destabilizing protein; high expression marks microtubule-addicted, antimitotic-sensitive lines
TP53-mutant lines dominate the sensitive set, suggesting impaired apoptosis checkpoints after mitotic arrest
MDR1 efflux of benzimidazoles reduces intracellular drug and tubulin engagement
cell-cycle checkpoint loss permits mitotic catastrophe after tubulin inhibition
EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines (HCC4006, KYSE270) are among least affected, suggesting survival signaling buffers antimitotic stress
BRAF-mutant melanoma/colorectal lines appear in the resistant set, possibly via MAPK-driven survival
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT survival signaling, reducing sensitivity to microtubule destabilization
KRAS-mutant lines are enriched among least affected, consistent with oncogenic survival signaling
proliferation marker downregulated by drug; high expression indicates mitotic dependence
mitotic kinase; high expression marks rapidly dividing, antimitotic-sensitive cells
mitotic ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme; high expression reflects mitotic addiction
